title: End-to-End Context Compression at Scale
authors: Ang Li, Sean McLeish, Haozhe Chen (equal contribution), Nimit Kalra, Zaiqian Chen, Artem Gazizov, Venkata Anoop Suhas Kumar Morisetty, Bhavya Kailkhura, Harshitha Menon, Zhuang Liu, Brian R. Bartoldson, Tom Goldstein, Sanae Lotfi, Micah Goldblum, Pavel Izmailov
lab: NYU, Modal Labs, University of Maryland, Princeton, Columbia, Harvard, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, FAIR at Meta (advisory only)
date: 8 June 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version as of 3 October 2026)

code.title: LeonLixyz/LCLM
code.note: training (four-stage pipeline from one YAML), Hugging Face and two-stage vLLM inference, and the EXPAND agent; the repository shows no licence (checked 3 October 2026), while the three checkpoints at huggingface.co/latent-context are Apache-2.0

takeaway: Revives encoder-decoder soft-token compression by arguing its weakness was training scale rather than architecture: a from-scratch architecture search settles the design (mean pooling over token pooling, encoder window 1024 rather than one block, causal encoder attention, plain MLP adapter), then a 0.6B encoder plus 4B decoder trained end to end on 350B tokens at 4x/8x/16x beats KV cache compression on the accuracy-versus-TTFT frontier by 5-9x, keeps a standard KV layout so it works in vLLM and SGLang, and supports an agent that skims a compressed codebase and calls EXPAND on the chunks it needs; scaling the decoder helps loss more than scaling the encoder.
verdict: Believe the systems result: shrinking the sequence before the decoder sees it cuts time and memory, by a lot at long context, and the released checkpoints let anyone check. Treat the quality claims more carefully: at 4x and 8x the slower KV methods are still more accurate on RULER, the 8.8x headline is measured against a baseline that is itself six times slower than not compressing at all, the 16x points in Figures 1 and 5 sit 1.5 to 2.8 points above the paper's own Table 6, and several architecture choices rest on single-run loss gaps of 0.003 to 0.02 that the downstream tables do not always confirm.

headline.k: peak memory of the 16x model from 128K to 512K tokens
headline.d: every KV method stops at 256K; uncompressed needs 119 GB there

resources.n: the RAG-specific version of the same idea, with precomputable chunk embeddings and an RL policy choosing what to expand; useful as the narrower, more deployable sibling (the paper cites it for W = N token pooling).

resources.t: Prompt Compression for Large Language Models: A Survey
resources.n: the map of the field this paper is arguing with, covering the gist, ICAE, AutoCompressor, 500xCompressor and xRAG lineage.

resources.t: KVzip: Query-Agnostic KV Cache Compression with Context Reconstruction
resources.n: the strongest KV baseline at 4x and 8x here; scores each cache entry by the attention it gets while the model reconstructs its own context.
the library whose SnapKV, KVzip, FastKVzip and Expected Attention implementations and timing notebook the paper uses for every baseline.

resources.t: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
resources.n: the synthetic suite behind the paper's headline: needle retrieval, multi-hop tracing, aggregation and QA, 13 tasks per length.
model cards with the configuration of each released model (encoder window 1024, mean pooling, causal encoder, MLP adapter, no overlap); Apache-2.0.

kb.n: the other route to spending more parameters on reading than writing, restructuring the model rather than compressing the input; the two disagree on whether the encoder should be causal.

kb.t: Trained Persistent Memory for Frozen Encoder-Decoder LLMs
kb.n: the same instinct applied to memory rather than input context, putting state in continuous latents so reads and writes are differentiable.

kb.t: Efficient Memory Management for LLM Serving with PagedAttention (vLLM)
kb.n: the KV cache layout this paper's baselines are constrained by, and the reason systems-realisability is a real distinction.
MLA compresses the KV cache inside attention, the same goal one layer down; it composes with this rather than competing.

kb.t: Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness
kb.n: the recursive-language-model direction the authors name as naturally compatible, where a compressed working memory is the substrate.

kb.t: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
kb.n: the other way to avoid a growing cache, a fixed-size recurrent state, with the same exact-recall cost that shows up here at high compression.
the encoder-decoder and the attention whose per-token KV cache this paper is trying to shrink.

kb.t: DeepSeek (deep dive, with the MLA animation)
kb.n: the KV cache arithmetic for latent attention, animated token by token.
